conviction_note: The reported quarter leans slightly good: Mexican construction ran +7% YoY through July and August against a weak Q3 2025 base, the peso traded about 17.0-17.5 against the company's own 18.25-18.50 assumption, and US shipments were firm with no Q3 hurricane. Against that, Brent went from $72 to about $104 by quarter end, after the 23 July guide, which points at the Q4 and 2027 cost commentary. The findings net to about -0.1 and p_up is 50; abs_move 4.5 comes from realised vol and confirmed past prints because there is no usable option chain.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $4.45bn and EPS $0.25 (MarketBeat, single source: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-cemex-cx-set-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/). Actinver expects EBITDA +10% YoY and revenue +1% (Bloomberg Linea, 2026-10-18: https://www.bloomberglinea.com/mercados/de-cemex-a-walmex-que-esperar-de-los-reportes-trimestrales-en-la-bolsa-mexicana/). The two revenue estimates do not agree: +1% on Q3 2025's ~$4.245bn is ~$4.29bn, against $4.45bn. Company guide (Q2 6-K, 2026-07-23: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001076378/000119312526313194/d46310dex1.htm): FY2026 EBITDA +16-17% like-for-like. On FY2025 EBITDA of $3.08bn that is ~$3.57-3.60bn. H1 2026 was $1,812M, so the implied H2 is ~$1.76-1.79bn, about +6-8% YoY, against +28% in H1. Q3 2025 EBITDA was $882M (Dow Jones, via search). The guide pace puts Q3 at roughly $940-950M; Actinver's +10% is about $970M, above it. The bar is not sourced to two agreeing estimates, so every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is low: about 10.0M ADS short, 1.8 days to cover (2026-07-15 settlement, aggregator citing FINRA: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cx/short-interest/), and 10.78M shares, 0.7% of shares outstanding, 2.43 days to cover on 2026-05-29 (https://equibles.com/stocks/cx/short-interest). No October settlement was found. Not a crowded short. Skew: none; the option chain is unusable (ATM spread 167% of mid, put/call OI 0.43, ATM IV 51%, which is not credible). Tape: spot $10.06, -25.8% from the 52-week high of $13.67 (2026-05-06), +7.8% off the low, 20d +3.6%, 5d -1.85%. The CPO was MXN 22.62 on the Q2 print day (https://gbm.com/media/noticia/acciones-mexicana-cemex-avanzan-tras-informe-trimestral/) and is now about MXN 18 implied (ADR $10.06 x ~17.8 MXN / 10 CPOs). So the stock has de-rated about 20% in local terms since the beat-and-raise, consistent with rates and energy fears already being in the price. Citi upgraded to Buy on 2026-10-14 while cutting its target to $12 from $13.70.

findings.finding: INEGI's industrial activity data show Mexican construction up 6.7% YoY seasonally adjusted (+7.3% in original figures, edificacion +8.2%) in July 2026 and +7.5% YoY in August 2026, with construction January-August at +3.5%. That is an acceleration in the first two months of Q3. It comes against a weak Q3 2025 base, when Cemex Mexico sales were -2% and FY2025 Mexican cement volumes -8%. Mexico was 48% of Q2 2026 EBITDA ($491M of $1,018M). Points to Mexican volumes at or above the sell-side's ~+1% revenue view; management guided only that H2 Mexico margins would be below H1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: 'Mexico continued to outperform expectations' (+12% lfl sales, +27% EBITDA). The CPO rose 2.0% intraday on the release (GBM), while the baseline ADR row for 2026-07-23 reads -3.62% (an untrusted history). Q3 2024: a weak quarter driven by Mexico sent the CPO down 8% (https://elceo.com/mercados/acciones-de-cemex-se-desploman-en-la-bmv-tras-debil-reporte-trimestral/).
findings.why_not_priced: The series is public, so this is partly priced. But management's own H2 framing was cautious ('reversal of temporary market share gains, a less favorable bag-to-bulk mix, maintenance outages and reduced energy tailwinds'), and Actinver's revenue estimate is only +1% YoY. If the market had priced a 7% construction acceleration in Mexico, revenue estimates would sit well above +1%, and the CPO would not be 20% below its Q2 print-day level.
findings.independence: A macro proxy, not company-confirmed. It is corroborated by Citi's 2026-10-14 upgrade citing 'early recovery in Mexican property markets' (https://ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/cemex-stock-citi-upgrades-cemex-to-buy-and-cuts-target-for-cemex-stock-to-usd-12-00/70394140), and by GCC's Q2 Mexico cement volumes +6.2% (https://norfolkdailynews.com/online_features/press_releases/gcc-reports-second-quarter-2026-results/article_cb32f15b-bee4-5583-ac6e-f739064357c3.html). It cuts against management's own warning about share-gain reversal, which reduces it.

findings.finding: The peso traded about MXN 17.4-17.5 per USD in July, ~17.0 in mid-August and ~16.9 in early September 2026, weakening only to ~17.8 in the last days of September. That is well stronger than the 18.25-18.50 the company assumed for H2 2026 in its Q2 guide. Peso revenue and EBITDA (Mexico, ~48% of group EBITDA) therefore translate into more USD than the guide's own FX deck implies. The FY growth guide is like-for-like, so the guide percentage is unaffected, but reported USD EBITDA and sales should land above a guide-anchored model.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No confirmed-release evidence that this name reacts to FX translation; it is normally looked through as non-operational.
findings.source_date: 2026-07-16 (with AlCierre 20260702, 202608014, 20260902 and the company assumption in the 2026-07-23 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001076378/000119312526313194/d46310dex1.htm)
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side models usually mark FX to spot, so most of this is likely in the $4.45bn revenue estimate. What would differ if it were fully priced: consensus revenue clearly above Q2's $4.59bn pace in Mexico. Actinver's +1% revenue view suggests at least one house did not. Small.
findings.independence: FX data is independent of the company. It shares no document with the INEGI finding, but both land on the Mexico line, so they are not fully additive.

findings.finding: Energy shock after the guide. Brent front-month began Q3 2026 at $72/b, passed $100 on 23 July (the day of the Q2 guide) and again on 9 September, peaked at $109 (spot $132) on 15 September, and averaged about $104 in the last two weeks of the quarter on Hormuz disruption. Distillate crack spreads were nearly triple year-ago levels. On 23 July management already flagged 'reduced energy tailwinds' for Mexico H2, but the September leg came after the guide. That raises the risk of cautious Q4/2027 cost commentary, or a lower end of the 16-17% EBITDA guide, from fuel, power and diesel freight.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No confirmed-release data in this window on energy-driven guide changes. The rebuilt base rate on confirmed prints is a beat-and-raise in Q2 2026 (CPO +2% intraday; untrusted ADR row -3.6%) and a Mexico-driven miss in Q3 2024 (CPO -8%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The ADR is -26% off its May high, the CPO is ~20% below its Q2 print-day level, and peers VMC and MLM fell ~3% on 2026-10-23. No source quantifies Cemex's fuel hedging, and Citi's 2026-10-14 note cut its target while upgrading. If the market had fully priced a guide cut, the stock would not have rallied +3.6% over 20 days into the print.
findings.independence: Macro-to-company transmission, not confirmed by the company beyond the 23 July 'reduced energy tailwinds' remark (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/cemex-q2-earnings-call-highlights). Shipping data agree: Ship & Bunker raised bunker outlooks on the EIA's Hormuz view (https://shipandbunker.com/news/world/341945-ship-bunker-raises-q4-bunker-price-outlook-by-112mt-as-eia-sees-brent-holding-near-90-through-year-end).

findings.finding: US demand was firm with no Q3 weather hit. USGS shipments of portland and blended cement were +9.8% YoY in June 2026 and +5.1% in H1 2026. The Atlantic season was one of the quietest in years, with no Texas or Florida hurricane landfall in July-September; Bertha was a tropical storm in Texas in July. Cemex US EBITDA was -11% in Q2 on unseasonable Texas weather, and management said H2 US margins would improve if hurricanes did not disrupt, which they did not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: US sales -2% but a record Q3 margin. Reaction not isolated to this line.
findings.source_date: 2026 (June data, published ~September 2026; date from the article context, not verified on page)
findings.why_not_priced: Industry data is public and July-August USGS data were not found, so this is mostly priced. US peers have not reported Q3 yet (VMC/MLM report later), so there is no counterparty confirmation in the market.
findings.independence: Proxy. GCC Q2 US cement volumes +10.8% (https://norfolkdailynews.com/online_features/press_releases/gcc-reports-second-quarter-2026-results/article_cb32f15b-bee4-5583-ac6e-f739064357c3.html); Amrize Q2 cement volumes +5% (https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/080726-amrize-raises-revenue-guidance-on-stronger-demand-from-data-centers).

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias made a Category 2 landfall near Destin, Florida in October 2026, the first direct US hurricane landfall in more than two years, with 400k+ outages. That is a possible Q4 disruption that could colour Q4 US commentary. Cemex's main Florida assets are in central and south Florida, not the Panhandle.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (from search snippet; exact day not verified)
findings.why_not_priced: Widely reported, so it is priced if material. Included only for completeness.

findings.finding: On 2026-07-20 the European Commission sent Cemex a Statement of Objections (case AT.40861) alleging coordination of construction-chemicals and admixture price increases in France, Germany and Spain in 2021-22. Q3 is the first quarter after the SO, so a provision or a contingency disclosure could appear. Cemex says its third-party chemicals sales are limited.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The SO news was reported as weighing on the shares in July 2026 (https://www.cronista.com/tema/cemex-mx/); not quantified.
findings.why_not_priced: The SO is known. Whether Cemex books a provision is not; a provision would be below EBITDA with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.

findings.finding: EMEA volumes are likely soft again. Buzzi's H1 2026 report shows German cement -3.5% and ready-mix -6.9% and expects H2 demand in line with H1. Cemex's own Q2 EMEA volumes were lower. And Q2 EMEA EBITDA (+24%) carried a $42M one-off settlement that will not repeat in Q3 (ex one-off +9%). EMEA was 29% of Q2 EBITDA.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EMEA weakness was offset by Mexico and the stock moved little. No isolated reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; the one-off was disclosed. Included because a model run off Q2's EMEA margin of 19.3% would overstate Q3.
findings.independence: Cemex's own Q2 6-K says EMEA was 'held back by lower volumes' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001076378/000119312526313194/d46310dex1.htm). That is a different document but the same direction.

findings.finding: Citi upgraded Cemex to Buy from Neutral on 2026-10-14, citing an early recovery in Mexican property, a stronger balance sheet and cost-program progress, while cutting its target to $12.00 from $13.70 on higher US rates. A sell-side house is turning constructive into the print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is wire copy and priced. It may be part of why the 20d run-up is +3.6%. Kept tiny.
findings.independence: It shares the Mexico-recovery thesis with the INEGI finding, so the two are not independent.

outside_window.finding: The Colombian divestment to Holcim ($485M, plus ~$70M of other nearby assets) is expected to close at year end, subject to regulatory approval. Deleveraging support, but it will not close inside the window; the call may only update timing.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The 20% local-currency de-rating since the Q2 beat-and-raise means energy and rate fears are largely in the price, which tempers both the negative guidance finding and the positive reported-quarter findings. The net is near zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 6: the bar is one source (MarketBeat) and disagrees with Actinver's revenue view, so every finding is kept capped small. That trimmed the Mexico construction proxy from +0.6 to +0.5 and the FX finding from +0.4 to +0.3.

Rule 5: macro-to-company transmission is filed small, not dropped. The energy finding went from -1.0 to -0.8 and the US shipments finding from +0.4 to +0.3; both independence fields say they are proxies.
Rule 3: management's own H2 Mexico caution is a caveat against the INEGI finding, so it is netted into that finding's size rather than counted again.
Lessons rule on untrusted FPI history: rebuilt the base rate from confirmed releases (Q2 2026 CPO +2% intraday, Q3 2024 CPO -8%) instead of using the baseline's 1.33% median; abs_move stays 4.5.
Rule 2: the EU antitrust provision stays a one_off at a fraction (-0.2), with no path to the guide.
p_up stays 50 and abs_move 4.5, so expected_move is unchanged at 0.0; the sum moves from 0.0 to -0.1.
